_comment: Places where twig.js knowingly differs from Twig PHP.
Each entry records the output twig.js actually produces and why that is
tolerated. An entry whose case starts agreeing FAILS the run, so a closed
gap has to be deleted here — that rule is what stops this file becoming a
graveyard of reasons nobody has revisited.
Adding an entry is a decision, not a formality. If the reason is only 'this
is hard to fix', it probably belongs in an issue instead.

if/empty-hash.reason: Twig.lib.boolval is locutus's, which reports {} as true. locutus's own convention reads a plain object as a PHP associative array (locutus.objectsAsArrays, on by default and honoured by is_array), and PHP calls an empty array falsy — boolval just never consults it. Correcting this reaches every if/and/or/ternary in the library, so it is deliberately out of scope for a comparison fix.

not/empty-hash.reason: Same boolval gap as if/empty-hash, seen through `not`.

num/float-sum.reason: PHP's `precision` ini (14 by default) truncates float output; JavaScript prints all 17 significant digits. Both hold the same IEEE 754 double — only the stringification differs. Matching PHP would mean reimplementing its float formatter, and because `precision` is deployment-configurable the target is not even fixed.

num/division-recurring.reason: Same float stringification difference as num/float-sum.

num/large-int.reason: Above 2^53 JavaScript numbers lose integer precision, where PHP has a 64-bit int type. A language-level difference, not a twig.js defect: fixing it needs BigInt throughout the expression evaluator.

num/large-exponent.reason: twig.js cannot parse scientific-notation literals at all — 1e20, 1E20, 1.5e3 and 1e-3 are all syntax errors. This is a parser gap and a real bug worth its own fix; the entry exists so the suite can land before that work does.

num/small-exponent.reason: Same scientific-notation parser gap as num/large-exponent.

num/abs-negative-float.reason: Filter-versus-unary-minus precedence. PHP's Twig binds `-1.5|abs` as `-(1.5|abs)`, so it prints -1.5; twig.js applies the filter to the negative literal. `(-1.5)|abs` agrees in both, so the divergence is in precedence, not in `abs` itself.

cmp/numeric-string-order.reason: '10' > '9' compares numerically in PHP because both operands are numeric strings; twig.js compares them as strings. The same PHP 8 rule the `==` fix implements, applied to the relational operators — worth fixing there next.

filter/sort-mixed.reason: PHP's sort() compares numeric strings numerically, so '10' sorts after 3; twig.js sorts lexically. Downstream of the same numeric-string rule as cmp/numeric-string-order.

filter/join-final.reason: twig.js's `join` ignores the second argument, the final separator Twig added in 2.x. A missing feature rather than a semantic difference.

filter/column.reason: The `column` filter is not implemented in twig.js.

filter/default-false.reason: `false|default('fallback')` returns the fallback in PHP, because `default` tests emptiness and PHP calls false empty. twig.js keeps false. Another face of the boolval gap, reached through a filter.

string/interpolation.reason: String interpolation with #{...} inside double quotes is not implemented in twig.js; the literal passes through untouched.

string/escaped-backslash.reason: twig.js does not collapse an escaped backslash inside a double-quoted literal, so \\ stays two characters where PHP renders one.
